memory_candidates.content: When a bash heredoc uses an UNQUOTED delimiter (<< PYEOF, not << 'PYEOF'), bash performs backtick command substitution on the heredoc body before handing it to the interpreter reading stdin. Markdown-style backticks in a Python docstring/comment inside such a heredoc (e.g. `sources/`, `doc_id`) get executed as shell commands, producing 'command not found' stderr noise even though the consuming program's stdout is unaffected. Check heredoc quoting style before adding backtick-quoted identifiers to any comment/docstring inside it.

When extending a fidelity/classification audit script to a second data schema, guard the write path against re-stamping entries that already carry a value OUTSIDE the script's own computed enum -- such a value likely came from a more specific, out-of-band assessment (manual curation, a different pipeline) and blanket-stamping with the generic detector's coarser classification silently downgrades information. Gate on 'is the current value one of MY possible outputs' before overwriting, not just 'does this entry match my target-selection criteria.'
